hero.title: Bindusara: The Second Mauryan Emperor
hero.description: Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, consolidated the vast Mauryan empire and maintained crucial diplomatic relations with the Hellenistic world.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The reign of Bindusara marks the bridge between Chandragupta's expansion and Ashoka's consolidation.

cards.details: Reign of Bindusara, known as Amitraghata (Slayer of foes) in Greek accounts (Amitrochates).

items.title: A.D.S
items.decryption: A for Amitraghata (Title), D for Deimachus (Ambassador from Antiochus I), S for Syrian trade (figs, wine, philosopher requested).

items: Confusing Bindusara with Bimbisara (Haryanka dynasty, contemporary of Buddha).
Assuming he conquered the South; evidence suggests his reign was mostly about maintaining the inherited empire.
Mistaking him for a staunch Buddhist; he was a follower of the Ajivika sect.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Consolidated empire from Pataliputra to the Deccan plateau.
  • Secured trade routes with the West.

Personalities

  • Antiochus I (Seleucid King)
  • Deimachus (Greek Envoy)
  • Dionysius (Envoy from Ptolemy II)

Core Governance & Foreign Policy

  • Diplomacy: Maintained the 'Seleucid-Mauryan' friendship; exchanged gifts (figs, wine, and philosopher).
  • Administration: Retained Chanakya as Chief Minister; utilized provincial viceroys (Kumara) in Taxila and Ujjain.
  • Religion: Patronized the Ajivika school; his mother Durdhara was a major influence.
